+Trader Interactive Unveils New Core, Pro & Ultimate Packages

+Trader Interactive has launched new Core, Pro and Ultimate dealer packages across RV Trader, Cycle Trader, Commercial Truck Trader and Equipment Trader, establishing a streamlined structure that delivers more value and stronger performance for dealers, Trader Interactive said in a release.

+The new packaging structure organizes Trader Interactive’s most impactful and innovative dealer tools into clear, performance-focused offerings to help dealers engage qualified buyers and manage inventory more effectively, the company said. Each level brings together merchandising enhancements, pricing intelligence, lead call analytics and AI optimization to make it easier for dealers to generate more value from the company’s marketplaces by increasing visibility and maximizing lead conversion for the dealer’s inventory.

+“These new packages combine our newest and most innovative retailing tools with the performance dealers expect and deserve,” said Roger Dunbar, chief operating officer at Trader Interactive. “Core, Pro and Ultimate each provide meaningful improvements to help dealers connect faster and with more buyers, manage inventory more efficiently and improve overall results.”
+The redesigned packages deliver the following dealer-focused benefits:
+Simplified package structure with Core, Pro and Ultimate tiers that align value with performance
+Enhanced visibility and merchandising through upgraded placements, listing badges and AI-driven merchandising tools, generating increased clicks to the vehicle detail page
+New Data-driven pricing and inventory intelligence powered by Pricing Insights and Inventory IQ to help move inventory faster
+New CallConnect transcription and summaries that record, transcribe and summarize every tracked call for insight into buyer intent in under 30 seconds
+Vehicle History Reports delivered only on qualified leads to build buyer trust and speed up closing, driving double-digit increases in overall lead volume
+Our improved AI Auto Selector automatically optimizes listing enhancements based on buyer behavior, increasing pageviews and leads by up to 15%

+Dealers adopting the new packages also receive complimentary access to Trader Interactive’s AI Lead Response Beta, an intelligent automation tool that sends instant replies to every email inquiry at all hours. The feature boosts engagement by ensuring dealers respond first, improves sales team efficiency and organizes buyer details for better follow-up. The Beta is available at no additional cost.

+The launch signals a broader shift in Trader Interactive’s strategy to modernize its marketplaces with data intelligence and practical AI tools that improve dealer performance, the company said. The new packages were shaped by dealer feedback and underscore the company’s focus on building products that increase lead quality, accelerate inventory turn and create a more efficient digital retail experience.

+Yes. Your reps will use Proton because it makes their day easier and helps them find more to sell. Compared to other CRMs and platforms, reps get value without much typing. They can ask Pronto, our AI chat agent, for a call plan, log notes by voice, and use the mobile app in the field to plan their sales routes and talk tracks. +Proton connects directly with any ERP, including Epicor P21, Epicor Eclipse, Infor SX.e, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics Business Central, and more. See more on our integrations page.
+Most companies are live in about 12 to 16 weeks, depending on size and the number of products. Adding a new branch or business unit at a company already using Proton is much faster.
+Our data is messy, or we’re changing ERPs. Should we wait?

+Proton’s real-time, two-way connection sends fixes made in Proton back into your ERP, so your data gets better the longer you use it. It works best when the person who knows your ERP data works closely with your product experts, since they’re the ones who can define what good data looks like.
+Changing ERPs? You can start on the system you have today. Proton’s data layer can connect to more than one ERP at a time, which is how acquired companies keep their own systems.
+Do I have to switch CRMs to use Proton?

+No. Proton connects directly to your ERP, so it works whether or not you already have a CRM. Some customers move their whole sales team to Proton. Others keep their current CRM and use both. Your reps will use Proton itself to see their recommendations, because Proton doesn’t run inside another CRM.
+Each product also works on its own, so you can start with product information management (PIM), order and quote automation, or eCommerce AI and keep your current CRM.

+Salesforce was made to be generic to fit the use cases of many industries. Proton is set up for distribution out of the box: accounts, branches, order history, quotes, and rebates. You don’t need a team of admins to build and maintain it. Proton’s AI also uses your ERP data to show reps which accounts are slipping and what to sell next, without anyone building reports first. +Can Proton handle project business and long sales cycles?
+Yes. You can set up pipeline stages to match how you sell, track several contractors’ bids under one parent opportunity, and store drawings and spec books with each project.
+Does order and quote automation work if we sell custom or configured products?

+Proton reads the request, matches what it can to your catalog, and suggests substitutes. A rep reviews every line before anything reaches the ERP, so your experts still decide what the customer gets.
+Can Pronto answer questions from our own documents?
+Yes. You can load spec books, warranty terms, safety standards, and internal guides into a knowledge base, and Pronto uses them alongside your ERP data when it answers.
+Where is our data hosted, and how is it secured?

We’re hosted on Google Cloud, encrypt customer data at rest and in transit, keep each customer’s data logically separated, and run quarterly vulnerability scans plus annual third-party penetration tests. In our Trust Center you’ll find our controls, certifications, subprocessors and AI model providers, and the documents a security review typically asks for.
